newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt sees SAA stake sale in 1998.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt sees SAA stake sale in 1998.

text.p: Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Monday that the government was likely to sell a strategic stake in national flag carrier South African Airways during 1998.

Updating parliament on plans for the restructuring and privatisation of state assets, Sigcau said the overhaul of SAA -- which faces increased competition from other airlines operating on its routes -- was a priority.

"The government's preferred method is to seek a strategic equity partner (SEP). Labour has shown support for the SEP route and government expects that the restructuring of SAA is expected to be complete during 1998," she said.
British Airways Plc and Deutsche Lufthansa AG are among companies to have expressed interest in acquiring a stake in SAA.

Sigcau said the SEP route was also the government's preferred option for the Airports Company which runs South Africa's main airports. The restructuring of this business was expected to be substantially complete by the end 1997 or early next year.
"It is expected that there will be keen interest from international airport operators to acquire a minority shareholding in the company," she added.
BAA Plc is one company which has already shown interest in the airports operator.
The restructuring of state forestry company Safcol, complicated by the issue of land claims, should be achieved in "some form" by the end of 1997 or early 1998, Sigcau said.

Land claims are also complicating the restructuring of been started for the sale of 100 percent of the equity. The government had previously predicted that this sale would be completed in 1997 but Sigcau it might now drag on into 1998.
Namaqualand diamond mine Alexkor should see restructuring -- which analysts expect to involve privatisation of up to 100 percent -- in late 1997 or early 1998.

The next concrete step in the South African government's tentative privatisation programme will come sale of 100 percent of regional airline Sun Air SNAJ.CN. Sigcau announced last month that eight bidders had been shortlisted to receive tender documents in May with the deal scheduled for completion in July or early August.

Sigcau was non-committal on the future of South Africa's biggest state company, electricity producer Eskom. Government had various options which it planned to discuss with stakeholders including labour -- an exercise which should be completed by August, she said.
Eskom gave no details on the timing of any Eskom changes, but officials said recently that any privatisation plans for the enterprise were on hold for two to three years.
The first stage of a wide-ranging review of the Transnet parastatal -- which includes SAA -- should be completed during May or June.
Within the Transnet stable, road transport group Autonet is a candidate for privatisation while the future of PX and Portnet is under review.
Defence company Denel was currently the subject of a consultant's study, Sigcau said.
